title: Bodycam Shows Miami-Dade Sergeant in Shootout With Armed Man
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Miami-Dade County, Florida — On September 16, 2025, Miami-Dade deputies were dispatched to the Goulds neighborhood after a series of urgent 911 calls reported a man threatening people with a gun near a local grocery store. Callers told dispatchers that a man inside a gray Honda Odyssey was pointing a firearm at passersby and causing panic in the area around Southwest 216th Street and 120th Avenue. Because the situation involved an armed suspect actively menacing the public, a Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office sergeant was among the first to respond.

When the sergeant arrived, he located the van and approached the driver, later identified as 44-year-old Jose Pineda Jr. The sergeant ordered him multiple times to show his hands, but Pineda refused and responded with a statement claiming he didn’t have any hands. Moments later, the encounter escalated instantly when both the sergeant and Pineda opened fire. The sergeant backed away while returning shots and took cover behind a nearby truck as bullets struck both vehicles. The gunfight ended when Pineda exited the van injured and collapsed, with his gun beside him. He was taken to the hospital but later died from his wounds. No deputies were hurt, and state investigators are now reviewing the shooting, as is standard protocol.
